lines:
Responsibilities: Anchors all portable-repository IO inside the exact selected project workspace, supplies cross-platform durable file primitives and descriptive Git/worktree facts, and preserves ordinary user/Git ownership of the files.
Owned ephemeral facts: ResolvedPortableRootV1 contains WorkspaceIdentityV1, handle/file identity, relative repository path, filesystem capability/durability verdict, case-sensitivity mode, and optional Git repository/worktree/branch/HEAD identifiers as descriptive metadata only. AtomicWriteReceiptV1 reports file and parent-directory durability. The adapter owns no canonical event or Git index state.
Ports: OpenAnchoredRead, CreateNewAndFsync, AtomicReplaceExpected, FsyncDirectory, ListControlledDirectory, AcquireBranchGuard, RevalidateRootIdentity, and ReadGitFacts. Portable internal paths are fixed-layout and reject symlink/reparse components. Expected-content guards are rechecked immediately before atomic replacement; branch guards coordinate local writers but never substitute for immutable parent/head claims across machines.
Filesystem/Git behavior: same-volume temp/write/fsync/rename and directory fsync are used; Windows replacement and sharing semantics receive dedicated implementations. Unsupported atomicity, removable/network filesystem limitations, case collisions, root replacement, partial sync, or Git conflict markers yield explicit read-only/degraded diagnostics. History order comes solely from parent hashes, branch ordinals, and head claims—not mtimes, commit dates, checkout order, or Git log order.
Boundary and security: all files remain visible inside the user-chosen workspace and may be edited, ignored, committed, merged, or deleted by the user/Git. Aworkit may read status/identity to explain coexistence but never invokes stage, commit, merge, push, pull, checkout, reset, or remote operations, and never auto-creates a Git commit.
NFRs/non-responsibilities: bounded/cancellable IO, crash-injection tests, path and durability observability, and Windows/Linux/macOS parity. No workspace authority claim, path-policy bypass, canonical-backend selection, data scrubbing, branch merging, artifact execution, or user-version-control automation.

data.name: Filesystem & Git Coexistence Adapter
data.technology: Rust cross-platform anchored filesystem adapter with read-only Git/worktree inspection
